correctness.rationale: Exact Markov transition matrices reduce all initial-state total variation errors to a single terminal CDF. A reflection inequality for independent decreasing waiting-time densities puts the true CDF strictly above the mean of the two Strang CDF products; an exact product factor fixes their order. Hyperbolic-sinc bias identities plus strict monotonicity establish each sign, iff 2:1 full-matrix exactness and the long-step asymptotic. The standalone 65-digit Decimal checker passed 3,937 supplementary comparisons; proof rather than finite grids gives universal quantification.

value.rationale: The smallest serial irreversible Markov chain has a genuine two-way Strang order choice. A uniform-in-time optimum for all starting probability rows, a fixed signed-bias phase diagram and an exact whole-matrix resonance at rate ratio 2 provide actionable splitting benchmarks beyond local commutator/truncation heuristics. The badly ordered error can be exponentially larger at long timesteps for fixed a>2b; this is not a claim for general reaction networks.
